newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag, BT have post-RWE plan.
newsitem.headline: Viag, BT have post-RWE plan.

text.p: British Telekom Plc and German utility Viag AG will stand by their plans to integrate their telecommunications activities despite the unexpected departure of RWE AG from the alliance, Viag chairman Georg Obermeier said on Thursday.

In remarks prepared for delivery at a news conference, Obermeier said the two would invest six billion marks in telecommunications over the next 10 years, of which 4.2 billion marks would be invested in mobile phone activities.
The pair plan for their telecommunications cooperation to break even starting in 2003, Obermeier said.
Viag will take a majority stake in the mobile phone alliance with BT, and 10 percent of the venture will be left available for a new partner, he said.
BT's European director Patrick Gallagher was also due to address the news conference.
Viag and BT will seek the fourth German E2 mobile telephone license, which the Postal Ministry will grant in February 1997.

The group will create 9,000 new jobs by 2001, Obermeier said. Viag and BT aim for a share of 20 percent of the German mobile phone market, and seven percent of the fixed-line market, he said, without giving target dates.

RWE's defection from the group on Wednesday to a rival alliance with Cable & Wireless and utility Veba AG appeared to leave BT weakened in Germany, particularly amid speculation that Viag could form closer ties to the RWE-Veba group.
RWE dropped out of the alliance with Viag and BT over differences in strategy and control of some of the company's subsidiaries.

RWE chairman Dietmar Kuhnt, speaking to reporters in Essen late on Wednesday, said there had been insurmountable differences over how to market the E2 mobile phone licence the companies were preparing to bid for.
But he indicated that RWE was frustrated by BT's strategy for Germany, which is restricted to the business market.

"Only powerful alliances with a broad and comprehensive product offering will survive," Kuhnt said. "Not just a select group of large customers, but the broad population should benefit from the opening of the telecommunications market."
Vebacom, the joint venture between Veba and Cable & Wireless, will take 51 percent of a new service company, called Servco, and 49 percent of a network company dubbed Netco.
RWE's contribution, a combination of material assets and cash, would total around 3.6 billion marks, while Vebacom's contribution to the venture will be 4.8 billion marks.
A holding company called RWECOM will be created in which RWE will hold 75 percent and Vebacom 25 percent. RWECOM in turn will hold 51 percent of Netco and 49 percent of Servco.

The new alliance creates a powerful competitor not only to Deutsche Telekom, but also to the DBKom alliance of Mannesmann AG, the German railway Deutsche Bahn AG and AT&T Corp, which has been considered the strongest of the newcomers.
